answer: Attention-vesting settlement queues. Agents earn queue priority only by completing unpredictable micro-tasks over hours; priority decays unless refreshed. Each transaction carries a jade ticket whose validity requires a recent vine of verified attention events, checked at settlement. Cheap parallel identities stall at the summit of queue depth, since maintaining N identities costs N times sustained labor. Attackers must spend real human-equivalent attention hours per identity, making mass sybils economically unviable before they ever transact.
